docs.title: Welcome to Upkapp
docs.text:
Welcome to the official documentation for Upkapp!

Whether you are a small business owner, a facility manager, a hobbyist, or a professional juggling a hundred different responsibilities, you know that keeping track of repetitive tasks is a full-time job in itself. Upkapp is here to change that.

Website: Upkapp

Our Mission: To give you the scheduling power of an industrial-grade Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) without the overwhelming complexity and high costs.

docs.title: The Problem We Solve
docs.text:
Every business has repetitive tasks that must be controlled. This isn't just about physical maintenance; it covers everything from renewing software licenses and tax compliance to managing vehicle fleets and safety inspections.

When these tasks slip through the cracks, the results are painful: * Financial Loss: Broken equipment, expired contracts, or wasted time. * Legal & Compliance Issues: Missed safety inspections, audits, or regulatory filings. * Managerial Burnout: The constant, exhausting mental load of trying to remember what needs to be done and when.

Upkapp removes this mental load. It is designed to be highly affordable and incredibly simple to use, while offering advanced scheduling and tracking features that standard calendar apps and basic to-do lists simply cannot handle.

docs.title: What Makes Upkapp Different?
docs.text:
Upkapp goes beyond standard date-based reminders. Our system is built on logic designed specifically for real-world upkeep:

  • Smart Status Prioritization: Our intelligent algorithm evaluates the contextual importance of a task. It weighs the scheduled due date against your required advance notification, ensuring a critical deadline (like a 10-day license renewal) appears above a routine chore (like a 2-day cleaning task).
  • Dynamic Scheduling: Upkapp can calculate your next due date based on when you actually finished the job, not when you were supposed to finish it.
  • Meter & Data Tracking: Trigger tasks based on actual usage—like vehicle mileage or machine operating hours—using our lightning-fast, 5-second update interface.
  • Automated Work Orders: Seamlessly generate and assign tasks to your users the moment they are due based on your Job configurations.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
Ready to take control of your repetitive tasks? We recommend following these steps to get up and running smoothly:

  1. Understand The Upkapp Logic: Learn how to organize your operations using our simple hierarchy of Groups, Items, and Jobs.
  2. Follow the Quick Start Guide: Set up your very first automated workflow in minutes.
  3. Explore Use Cases: Get inspired by how other industries and professionals are using Upkapp to streamline their operations.

Navigate through the sidebar menu to find detailed guides, tutorials, and explanations for every feature Upkapp has to offer.

docs.title: User Assignments
docs.text: To ensure absolute accountability, every automated task in Upkapp can be tracked back to a specific person. Assigning a responsible user to your work orders eliminates confusion about who is executing a task, allowing your team to focus entirely on their daily duties.

docs.title: Filtering and Saved Views
docs.text:
The main Work Orders dashboard is built to accommodate both managers who need a bird's-eye view and team members who just need to see their own tasks.

  • Flexible Filtering: Users can filter the active dashboard to see only work orders assigned specifically to them, or filter by any other team member to check on workloads.

  • Preferred Saved Views: If you prefer to log in and immediately see only your own work orders, or if a manager always wants to see a specific department's work orders, you can save your customized filters as a Preferred View. Once saved, Upkapp will automatically load this specific visualization every time you open the dashboard.

docs.title: Granular Assignment Hierarchy
docs.text:
Upkapp gives you complete flexibility over how tasks are assigned. You don't have to manually attach a user to every single work order. Instead, you can define responsibility at different levels of the system.

The rule of thumb in Upkapp is simple: More granular (specific) options always override more generic ones.

Here is how the hierarchy works, from most generic to most specific:

  1. Item Level (The Baseline): You can assign a responsible user directly to an Item (e.g., assigning John Doe to Delivery Van A). Any Job created under this item will automatically default to John Doe.
  2. Job Level (The Rule Override): If a specific task on that item requires a specialist, you can override the baseline at the Job level.
    • Example: Even though John Doe is responsible for Delivery Van A, you configure the Annual Brake Overhaul Job to be automatically assigned to Jane Smith (the company mechanic). Upkapp will automatically route that specific work order to Jane, while all other routine van tasks still go to John.
  3. Work Order Level (The Instance Override): If a generated task is already live on the dashboard but needs to change hands due to a vacation, sick leave, or scheduling conflict, a manager can manually reassign that single specific Work Order. This changes the responsibility for this instance only without affecting the core Job rules.

docs.title: ⚠️ Important: Responsibility vs. Access Control
docs.text:
It is vital to understand that being assigned as the Responsible User for a task is entirely independent of system Access Rights.

  • User Assignment: Dictates who is expected to perform the physical work or monitor that specific task.
  • Access Rights (Permissions): Determines what data a user is allowed to see in the software. Upkapp manages visibility and access permissions at the Group level.

For example: A user can only see or filter work orders for Items that belong to a Group they have been granted access to. If they do not have access to the Finance Group, they will never see finance-related work orders, even if someone tries to assign one to them.

docs.title: Billing & Subscription
docs.text: At Upkapp, we believe in keeping our business model as straightforward and transparent as our software. Managing your subscription, updating payment methods, and downloading your invoices can all be done directly from your administration dashboard.

docs.title: Secure Payments via Stripe
docs.text:
Your financial security is our top priority. Upkapp uses Stripe to process all transactions. Stripe is a global leader in payment processing, ensuring your data is handled with the highest standards of industrial encryption and compliance.

  • Local Currency Support: In most cases, Stripe automatically processes your subscription in your country's local currency, saving you from unexpected international transaction fees or exchange rate surprises.
  • Accepted Methods: We support all major credit cards and alternative payment methods natively integrated through Stripe, like link.

docs.title: Flexible Subscription Model
docs.text:
We earn your business every month. Upkapp does not have lock-in contracts or long-term commitments.

  • Cancel Anytime: You can cancel your subscription at any moment with a single click from your account panel.

  • Fair Access: If you choose to cancel, your access to Upkapp remains completely active until the end of your current billing period, after which no further charges will be made.

docs.title: Plan Inclusions & Features
docs.text:
The core engine that makes Upkapp shine—such as Dynamic Scheduling, Meter Tracking, and our Smart Status Algorithm—is included in every single plan. We do not hide our best automation features behind expensive enterprise tiers.

Variations between plans typically depend on: 1. User Seats: The number of team members you can add to your account (our base plan includes 5 users). 2. Billing Cycles: Monthly subscriptions versus discounted annual commitments. 3. Advanced Integrations (Fancy Features): Specific premium add-ons, such as automated notifications sent directly to your team via WhatsApp, SMS alerts, or upcoming integrations with third-party software.

docs.title: How to Manage Your Billing
docs.text: Only the account owner (Master User) can access billing options.

docs.title: Updating Payment Info or Downloading Invoices
docs.text:
1. Log in to your Upkapp account as the Master User.
  2. Navigate to settings > Billing & Subscription.
  3. Click on Manage Billing. This securely redirects you to your dedicated Stripe customer portal.
  4. From here, you can:
    • Add, change, or remove credit cards.
    • View your complete payment history.
    • Download official invoices/receipts for your company's accounting department.

docs.title: The Upkapp Logic: Core Concepts
docs.text:
To get the most out of Upkapp, it is essential to understand the underlying logic of the system. While many apps just use a flat list of tasks, Upkapp uses a structured hierarchy designed to handle the complexity of real-world business operations without creating clutter.

Everything in Upkapp flows through a simple, four-tier structure: Groups > Items > Jobs > Work Orders.

docs.title: 1. Groups (The Categories)
docs.text: Groups are your top-level organizational folders. They define the broad areas of your business or life that require control and oversight. * Examples: Security, Facilities, Fleet, Finance, Compliance, IT Infrastructure.

docs.title: 2. Items (The Targets)
docs.text: An Item lives inside a Group. It represents the specific asset, logical division, or topic that requires maintenance or repetitive action. Items are highly flexible and don't just have to be physical machines. * Physical Examples: Delivery Van, Main Elevator, HVAC System, Fire Extinguisher. * Logical Examples: Q3 Taxes, Corporate Passports, Marketing Reports, Facility Leases.

docs.title: 3. Jobs (The Rules)
docs.text: Jobs are the engine of Upkapp. A Job is attached to an Item and defines the configuration of the repetitive task. It tells the system what needs to be done and exactly when or how often it should happen. * Examples: "Annual Engine Revision," "Renew License Every 5 Years," "Monthly Oil Check." * Counters & Meters: Jobs don't just run on dates. You can link a Job to a numeric counter (like mileage or hours of use). Upkapp provides a fast, 5-second interface to update these meters, and the system will automatically trigger the task when the target number is reached. It's possible to update counters using our API.

docs.title: 4. Work Orders (The Action)
docs.text: While Jobs are the rules, Work Orders are the actual, actionable tasks generated by those rules. When a Job's criteria are met (a date arrives or a meter hits its target), Upkapp automatically creates a Work Order. You execute the work, mark the Work Order as complete, and the system instantly looks at the Job's configuration to calculate and schedule the next Work Order.

docs.title: Putting It All Together: An Example
docs.text:
Let's look at how this hierarchy translates into a real-world scenario. Imagine you need to manage your building's fire safety.

Here is how you would map it out in Upkapp:

  • Group: Security
    • Item: Fire Protection System
      • Job A: Monthly Extinguisher Validity Check
      • Job B: Annual Leakage Test

How the automation works: Because you created "Job A," Upkapp will automatically generate a Work Order for the "Monthly Extinguisher Validity Check." When your team inspects the extinguishers and clicks "Complete" on that Work Order, Upkapp immediately creates a new Work Order for exactly one month later.

By structuring your data this way, you gain the power of an industrial tracking system, but with the simplicity of a clean, organized, and automated interface.

docs.title: Dynamic Scheduling
docs.text:
In standard calendar apps and basic to-do lists, recurring tasks are rigid. If a task is due on the 1st of the month and you complete it late on the 10th, the next instance remains fixed for the 1st of the following month, ignoring reality.

Upkapp solves this real-world operational problem with Dynamic Scheduling. When enabled, our system calculates the next work order due date based on the actual completion date of the previous work order, rather than the originally planned date.

docs.title: Static vs. Dynamic Scheduling
docs.text: Understanding when to use each scheduling mode is key to automating your business workflow effectively:

docs.title: Static (Fixed) Scheduling
docs.text: The next due date is anchored to a fixed calendar schedule, regardless of when or if the previous task was completed. * Best for: Tax deadlines, legal compliance, quarterly board meetings, or any task attached to a hard regulatory date. * Example: If corporate taxes are due on the 15th of every month, it does not matter if you file them early on the 10th or exactly on the 15th; the next deadline is always fixed for the 15th of the following month.

docs.title: Dynamic Scheduling
docs.text: The clock resets only after the work is actually done. The next due date shifts dynamically relative to the completion day. * Best for: Preventive maintenance, cleaning routines, inspections, or any upkeep task where the interval between actions is what truly matters. * Example: Building facade cleaning or equipment calibration.

docs.title: The Facade Cleaning Scenario
docs.text:
To see the power of Dynamic Scheduling in practice, imagine you need to clean your building's facade every 15 days.

Here is how the two modes handle a delayed task:

Scheduling Mode Original Due Date Actual Completion Next Due Date Static Mode October 1st October 5th (4 days late) October 15th (Only 10 days of gap left!) Dynamic Mode October 1st October 5th (4 days late) October 20th (Full 15 days from the actual completion)

docs.title: Why this matters:
docs.text:
In Static Mode, delaying a task crowds your schedule, forcing your team to perform the next cleaning just 10 days later, wasting time and resources.

In Dynamic Mode, Upkapp ensures you always maintain a realistic, safe, and cost-effective operational cadence without penalizing your team for unexpected delays.

docs.title: How to Enable Dynamic Scheduling
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Items and select your asset.
  2. Create a new Job or edit an existing one.
  3. Locate the Scheduling Mode options.
  4. Select Dynamic Recurrence.
  5. Input your frequency interval (e.g., every 15 days).
  6. Click Save.

From now on, the exact moment a user marks the active Work Order as Complete, Upkapp's algorithm automatically reads the completion timestamp, adds your defined interval, and seamlessly schedules the perfect next deadline.

docs.title: Groups
docs.text:
Groups represent the highest organizational tier in Upkapp. They function as broad categories or virtual folders, allowing you to segment and organize your control items according to your business structure, departments, or operational areas.

By separating your assets and responsibilities into distinct Groups, you eliminate dashboard clutter and make it easy for your team to navigate the system.

docs.title: Why Are Groups Important?
docs.text:
In a growing business, the number of items requiring repetitive tracking can quickly scale into the dozens or hundreds. Without proper categorization, finding a specific task becomes difficult.

Groups solve this problem by: * Improving Visibility: Filter your dashboard to focus only on a specific department (e.g., viewing only "Fleet" items while ignoring "Finance"). * Organizing Responsibilities: Align your Upkapp workspace with your actual company departments (e.g., Legal, Maintenance, IT). * Simplifying Navigation: Keep your sidebar and menus clean and structured. * Allowing access control: You can set permissions for each group, allowing only authorized users to view or edit items and work orders within that group.

docs.title: Strategic Examples of Groups
docs.text:
You can structure your Groups in whatever way best mirrors your organization. Here are some common blueprints based on different use cases:

Group Name What It Controls (Items) Facilities Main Office, Warehouse, Elevator, HVAC System Fleet Management Delivery Van A, Executive Sedan, Forklift #2 Security & Safety Fire Extinguishers, Alarm System, Emergency Exits Finance & Legal Q3 Tax Filing, Software Licenses, Corporate Insurance Human Resources Employee Onboarding Reviews, Certification Renewals

docs.title: Creating a New Group
docs.text:
1. Navigate to the Groups option in the main navigation menu.
  2. Click the Create New Group button in the top right corner.
  3. Enter a concise and descriptive name for the group.
  4. Click Save.

docs.title: Editing or Deleting a Group
docs.text:
• To Edit: Click on the specific Group, select Edit, modify the name, and save your changes.
  • To Delete: Click the delete icon next to the Group.
  • Note: Before deleting a Group, ensure you have reassigned or deleted any Items associated with it, as items cannot exist without a parent Group. If you delete a group, all items and work orders within that group will moved to a default group.

docs.title: Items
docs.text:
Items live directly inside Groups and represent the specific targets of your repetitive tasks and tracking. In Upkapp, an Item is a highly flexible concept: it can be a physical asset that requires maintenance, or a logical division (such as a legal or financial topic) that requires regular oversight.

By defining your Items clearly, you map out exactly what needs attention within your business operations.

docs.title: Physical Assets vs. Logical Divisions
docs.text: Unlike rigid industrial software that only tracks physical machinery, Upkapp allows you to track anything that demands routine control.

docs.title: Physical Items (Assets)
docs.text: These are tangible pieces of equipment, vehicles, or property that require hands-on upkeep to function correctly and safely. * Examples: Delivery Van #1, Main Server Rack, Office HVAC Unit, Forklift B.

docs.title: Logical Items (Topics/Divisions)
docs.text: These are intangible areas of responsibility, compliance requirements, or business processes that must be reviewed periodically to avoid legal or financial penalties. * Examples: Software Licenses, Corporate Passports, Monthly Accounting, Trademark Renewals.

docs.title: Strategic Structure Examples
docs.text:
To help visualize how Items fit into your workflow, look at how they connect to their parent Groups:

  • Group: Security
    • Item: Fire Protection System
    • Item: CCTV & Alarms
  • Group: Fleet
    • Item: Delivery Van A
    • Item: Forklift #2
  • Group: Finance & Legal
    • Item: Tax Compliance
    • Item: Commercial Leases

docs.title: Creating a New Item
docs.text:
1. Navigate to the Items section in the main menu.
  2. Click the Add Item button.
  3. Name: Enter a clear name for the Item (e.g., Main Office Elevator).
  4. Group Assignment: Select the appropriate parent Group from the dropdown menu (e.g., Facilities).
  5. Description (Optional): Add extra context, such as serial numbers, model types, or specific notes that will help your team.
  6. Click Save

Tip: Upkapp has info icons all over the app to quickly explain what each field means.

docs.title: Editing or Moving an Item
docs.text:
If your company structure changes, you can easily modify your Items: * Open the Item from your dashboard and click Edit. * You can update its name, description, or even change its parent Group if you need to reclassify it.

What's Next? Once you have created an Item, you are ready to configure the automated rules that will monitor it. Advance to the Jobs section to learn how to set up recurring schedules and tasks for your items.

docs.title: Jobs
docs.text:
Jobs are the engine of Upkapp's automation. A Job is a set of recurring rules attached to an Item that answers three critical questions: What needs to be done?, How often should it happen?, and Who should do it?

Instead of manually adding tasks to a calendar every month, you configure a Job once, and Upkapp takes care of the rest—automatically generating actionable Work Orders forever.

docs.title: The Anatomy of a Job
docs.text:
When you create a Job, you define the parameters that Upkapp will use to monitor your assets and operations. Every Job consists of:

  • Task Details: A clear title and instructions describing the work that must be performed.
  • Trigger Types: The rule that determines when a new task is due. This can be based on calendar time, usage data via Meters, or both.
  • Scheduling Mode: Choose between standard calendar logic or Upkapp's advanced Dynamic Scheduling engine.
  • cost control: You can set a cost for the job, and Upkapp will track the cost of each work order.

docs.title: Types of Job Triggers
docs.text: Upkapp offers complete flexibility by letting you automate tasks using two distinct trigger methods:

docs.title: 1. Time-Based Triggers (Calendar)
docs.text: Triggers a task based on a fixed time interval. * Examples: Check fire extinguisher validity every 30 days; file corporate tax returns every 3 months; conduct an executive strategy review annually.

docs.title: 2. Counter/Meter-Based Triggers (Usage)
docs.text: Triggers a task based on real-world usage metrics rather than calendar dates. You link the Job to an independent counter (like mileage or hours of operation). * Examples: Change engine oil every 5,000 miles; service an air compressor every 500 operating hours. * Note: Upkapp features a lightning-fast, 5-second quick-update interface specifically designed to keep these counters effortless to maintain.

docs.title: How to Configure a Job
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Items and select the specific Item you want to set up a task for.
  2. Inside the Item's dashboard, click the add new Job button.
  3. Name the Job: Use an action-oriented title (e.g., Deep Clean A/C Filters).
  4. Set the Trigger: * Choose Time Interval and input the frequency (days/weeks/months/years), OR
    • Choose Meter Counter and select the pre-configured Meter and target interval.
  5. Select Scheduling Mode: Choose between Standard or Dynamic Scheduling.
  6. Assign User (Optional): Select a team member to automatically receive this task.
  7. Click

Job Configured ──> (Auto-Generates) ──> Active Work Order

Marked Complete ──> (Instantly Calculates) ──> New Work Order

When a user completes that active Work Order, Upkapp immediately archives it for your compliance history, evaluates the Job's rules again, and seamlessly schedules the next Work Order. No manual rebuilding required.

docs.title: Meter & Data Tracking
docs.text:
While many maintenance tasks are based on the calendar, some of the most critical upkeep routines depend entirely on actual usage. Tracking tasks by calendar dates when they should be measured by wear-and-tear leads to over-maintenance (wasting money) or under-maintenance (causing breakdowns).

Upkapp solves this with Meters & Data Tracking, allowing you to trigger repetitive tasks based on independent counters like mileage, hours of operation, production cycles, or any custom metric.

docs.title: What is a Meter or counter?
docs.text:
A Meter in Upkapp is an independent counter that you create and associate with one or more Jobs. Instead of counting days, Upkapp counts units of use.

Common examples of Meters include: * Mileage (Odometer): For delivery vans, corporate cars, or trucks. * Operating Hours (Hour Meter): For air compressors, forklifts, generators, or industrial machinery. * Production Cycles/Clicks: For printing machines, injection molds, or automated equipment. * Elapsed Quantities: Any custom numeric data that increments over time.

docs.title: The 5-Second Quick Update Interface
docs.text:
The biggest failure of traditional asset management systems is that updating counters is tedious, so teams stop doing it. Upkapp eliminates this friction with our proprietary Quick Update Interface.

You do not need to navigate through complex asset sheets just to log a number. Upkapp provides a streamlined dashboard where updating any meter takes exactly 2 clicks and 5 seconds:

  1. Click the Update Counters floating action or tab.
  2. Type the new current value next to the asset (e.g., entering 45200 for a van's mileage) and hit enter.

The system instantly saves the data, updates the history, and evaluates all linked jobs in the background.

docs.title: Developer-Friendly: Automated Updates via API
docs.text: If your business uses IoT sensors, GPS/telematics tracking software, smart machinery, or custom internal systems, you do not need to type numbers manually at all. Upkapp offers a powerful API that allows you to automatically push meter readings from your existing software directly into Upkapp in real-time.

docs.title: How to Set Up Meter Tracking
docs.text: Automating a usage-based workflow involves two simple parts: creating the meter and linking it to a job.

docs.title: Step 1: Create the Meter
docs.text:
1. Go to the Meters section in the main navigation menu.
  2. Click Create New Meter.
  3. Give it a clear name (e.g., Van A Mileage or Forklift #2 Hours).
  4. Set the Unit of Measurement (e.g., Miles, Hours, Cycles).
  5. Input the Current Value to set your baseline starting point and click Save.

docs.title: Step 2: Link the Meter to a Job
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Items and open the asset you want to control (e.g., Delivery Van A).
  2. Click Create Job (or edit an existing one).
  3. Under Trigger Type, change it from Time-Based to Meter/Counter.
  4. Select the specific Meter you created in Step 1 from the dropdown menu.
  5. Set the Frequency Interval (e.g., trigger this job every 5,000 miles).
  6. Click Save.

docs.title: Real-World Example: Fleet Maintenance
docs.text:
Imagine you manage a transport van. You configure the system like this:

  • Meter: Van Mileage (Current baseline: 10,000 miles).
  • Job Linked: Change Engine Oil (Set to trigger every 5,000 miles).

How Upkapp Automates This: * The system knows the next oil change is due when the meter hits 15,000 miles. * Every Friday, your driver uses the 5-second interface to type in the current odometer reading. * Once the driver enters a value of 15,002, Upkapp automatically fires a Work Order titled Change Engine Oil directly to your maintenance team's dashboard. * When the task is completed, the system dynamically resets the target, preparing to trigger the next work order automatically at 20,002 miles.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text: Staying on top of your operations shouldn't require logging into a dashboard every hour. Upkapp keeps your team aligned and accountable by sending automated, high-level summaries of active tasks directly to any designated email inbox.

docs.title: What are Upkapp Notifications?
docs.text:
Notifications in Upkapp are scheduled email digests that summarize active Work Orders requiring attention. Instead of sending a separate, annoying alert for every single task update, Upkapp compiles everything into a clean, actionable overview.

To ensure strict control over account communication, only the Master User (the account creator) has permission to create and manage notification configurations.

💡 Ultimate Flexibility: You are not limited to just one notification setup. You can create multiple notification configurations tailored to different departments, managers, or schedules within a single Upkapp account.

docs.title: How to Create a Notification Rule
docs.text: To set up a new email digest, navigate to Menu > Settings > Notifications and configure the following parameters:

docs.title: 1. Name (Reference)
docs.text: Give your notification configuration a clear, recognizable name (e.g., Finance Department Summary or Weekly Fleet Overview). This name will appear in the subject line or header of the email so recipients instantly know the context.

docs.title: 2. Frequency & Timing
docs.text: Choose how often the email summary should be sent: * Daily: Sent every single day to keep tight control over fast-moving operations. * Weekly: Sent once a week. When selected, you can specify the exact day of the week you want the digest to fire (e.g., every Monday morning).

docs.title: 3. Status Filtering
docs.text: Select which specific work order statuses should be included in the email summary. * Note: Because the main purpose of this digest is to prompt action, completed or inactive statuses—such as Cancelled, Done, and Skipped—are deliberately unavailable for notifications.

docs.title: 4. Group Filtering
docs.text: Target the notification to specific areas of your business by checking the appropriate Groups. For example, you can route a "Facilities" notification only to your maintenance team. * Pro Tip: If you want the email to include absolutely everything across your entire company, simply leave the group selection blank to send data from all Groups.

docs.title: 5. Recipients
docs.text: Add the email addresses of the people who need to receive this summary. You can input any valid email address—recipients do not necessarily need to be registered Upkapp users, making this perfect for keeping external stakeholders, clients, or upper management informed.

docs.title: Practical Example: Multi-Notification Setup
docs.text:
Because you can create multiple rules, a typical business might structure their Upkapp notifications like this:

  • Notification 1: "Daily Leadership Alert"
    • Frequency: Daily
    • Statuses: Late
    • Groups: All Groups (left blank)
    • Recipients: CEO and COO emails.
  • Notification 2: "Weekly Maintenance Overview"
    • Frequency: Weekly (Mondays)
    • Statuses: Not Started, Started, Upcoming
    • Groups: Facilities, Fleet Operations
    • Recipients: Maintenance Supervisor and external workshop partner emails.

docs.title: Quick Start Guide
docs.text:
Getting started with Upkapp is designed to be fast and intuitive. In just a few minutes, you can set up your first automated workflow and start taking the mental load off your daily operations.

Follow these four simple steps to experience the core logic of Upkapp and automate your first repetitive task.

docs.title: Step 1: Create a Group
docs.text:
Groups are the highest level of organization in Upkapp. They act as broad categories or folders for the things you want to track and maintain.

  1. Navigate to the Groups tab in your main menu.
  2. Click the Create New Group button.
  3. Enter a name for your group (for example, Vehicles, Facilities, or Compliance) and click save.

docs.title: Step 2: Add an Item
docs.text:
Items live inside Groups. An Item is the specific target of your maintenance or task. It can be a physical asset or a logical division.

  1. Go to the Items section on menu or click on your group created.
  2. Click Add Item.
  3. Name your Item (for example, Delivery Van A, Main Office Elevator, or accountability).
  4. Select the Group you created in Step 1 from the dropdown menu to link them together.
  5. Fill optional fields when needed.
  6. Save your new Item.

docs.title: Step 3: Configure a Job
docs.text:
Jobs are the heart of Upkapp's automation. A Job defines the specific, repetitive work that needs to be done for an Item, and how often it happens.

  1. Open the Item you just created.
  2. Click on the Create Job button.
  3. Name the Job clearly (for example, Change Engine Oil, Annual Safety Inspection, or Renew Software License).
  4. Set your recurrence rule typing naturally onde apporprieted field. you can always ask for help click on "info" icon all over the app.
  5. Save the Job configuration.

docs.title: Step 4: Manage Your First Work Order
docs.text:
Once a Job is saved, Upkapp's engine goes to work. Based on the rules you just set, the system automatically generates an actionable Work Order.

  1. Navigate to your Work Orders page.
  2. Locate the newly generated Work Order for your Job automatically priorized by Upkapp's Smart Status. You can see more info here.
  3. Once the actual task is performed in real life, open the Work Order and click Complete.

The exact moment you mark that Work Order as complete, Upkapp instantly calculates and creates the next Work Order based on your Job rules. You have successfully automated your first task!

docs.title: Restarting a Job
docs.text:
In Upkapp, a Job defines the recurring rules that automatically generate your work orders. However, there are times when plans change mid-way, and you need to adjust your operational course. This is where the Restart Job feature comes in.

Restarting a Job allows you to safely reset a recurring cycle without losing your historical data.

docs.title: What Happens When You Restart a Job?
docs.text: When you execute a restart: * Active Task Cancellation: The system automatically cancels the current pending or active Work Order for that specific Job. * New Cycle Point: Upkapp instantly initiates a brand-new cycle from scratch, calculated dynamically from the new start date you configure. * History Preservation: Importantly, restarting does not erase the past. All previously completed work orders, logs, and compliance records remain completely safe and securely documented. You are simply establishing a new point of origin for the future.

docs.title: Common Use Cases
docs.text: There are two primary scenarios where you will need to restart a Job:

docs.title: 1. Significant Configuration Changes
docs.text: If your operational rules change drastically (e.g., shifting a maintenance routine from every 30 days to every 15 days, or changing the assigned specialist), it no longer makes sense to complete the old pending task under the old rules. By editing the Job and restarting it, you force the new configurations to take effect immediately based on your new chosen start date.

docs.title: 2. After Importing Templates
docs.text: Upkapp allows you to import pre-built task templates to accelerate your setup. However, these imported templates arrive with generic baseline start dates. Right after importing, you should review these Jobs and restart them, configuring the exact real-world date when that specific routine should officially begin for your business.

docs.title: How to Restart a Job
docs.text:
Executing a restart is simple and takes just a few clicks:

  1. Navigate to your Items or Jobs dashboard and click on the specific Job you wish to restart.
  2. Modify the Start Date and update any other configurations or rules as needed.
  3. Click on the arrow menu directly next to the Save button and select Save and Restart.
  4. A confirmation prompt will appear. Click Restart to confirm.

Think of restarting a Job as an intelligent, secure reset button that aligns your automated scheduling perfectly with your current business reality.

docs.title: Smart Status & Task Prioritization
docs.text:
In typical task managers and calendars, items are sorted strictly by their scheduled due date. While this works for simple, linear to-do lists, it fails in business operations. A routine, low-impact task due tomorrow can easily push a critical, high-impact deadline due in a week completely out of sight.

Upkapp solves this real-world operational issue with Smart Status, an intelligent prioritization algorithm that evaluates the contextual importance of each task, ensuring your most critical actions always rise to the top of your dashboard.

docs.title: How the Smart Status Algorithm Works
docs.text:
Instead of looking only at the calendar deadline, Upkapp's algorithm continuously calculates an urgency score by weighing two distinct factors:

  1. The Due Date: The final date by which the task must be completed.
  2. The Advance Notice Window: A user-defined period that dictates how early you need to start preparing for, or be aware of, a specific task.

By analyzing the ratio between the remaining time and your custom advance notice window, Upkapp determines which tasks represent the highest operational risk and dynamically rearranges your dashboard list.

docs.title: The Passport vs. Trash Example
docs.text:
To see the power of Smart Status in action, consider how the algorithm evaluates two very different tasks on a manager's dashboard at the same moment:

  • Task A (Routine): Weekly Office Waste Disposal
    • Due in: 2 days.
    • Advance Notice Window: 1 day.
    • Context: It is a quick, low-impact task that requires no preparation.
  • Task B (Critical): Renew International Corporate Passport
    • Due in: 10 days.
    • Advance Notice Window: 30 days (because passport renewal involves bureaucracy and weeks of processing time).
    • Context: Missing this deadline halts critical international business travel.

docs.title: The Sorting Comparison:
docs.text:
Dashboard View Top Priority (Rank #1) Second Priority (Rank #2) Standard Calendar Apps Task A: Waste Disposal (Due in 2 days) Task B: Passport Renewal (Due in 10 days) Upkapp Smart Status Task B: Passport Renewal (Deep inside its critical preparation window) Task A: Waste Disposal (Normal routine cycle)

Why this makes a difference: Standard apps hide the passport renewal because it is 10 days away, causing managers to forget about it until it is too late. Upkapp recognizes that because the passport requires 30 days of advance notice, having only 10 days left means you are already running out of preparation time. It safely forces the passport to the top of your list.

docs.title: Understanding Work Order Statuses
docs.text:
As work orders move through their lifecycle and the Smart Status algorithm evaluates them, they are assigned specific operational statuses. Upkapp dynamically sorts your dashboard based on these statuses, displaying them from the highest priority to lowest priority:

  1. Late: The scheduled due date has passed, and no action has been taken yet. This demands immediate attention to avoid operational, financial, or legal consequences.
  2. Not started: The wor order is now due but did not reach deadline to complete
  3. Started: The team has acknowledged the task and active work has officially begun within the scheduled timeframe and did not reacj deadline to complete.
  4. Started late: Work is started, not completed and have reached deadline.
  5. Upcoming: The task is approaching and has just crossed into your user-defined advance notice window, signaling that it is time to start planning or preparing for it.
  6. Scheduled: The task is safely planned for the future and currently sits well outside its advance notice window, requiring no immediate action.
  7. Cancelled: The specific work order was intentionally aborted and will not be executed during this cycle.
  8. Skipped: This specific work order was intentionally skipped. The system logs the skip for transparency and automatically focuses on the next scheduled cycle.
  9. Done: The work order has been successfully completed, verified, and closed out. The system immediately archives this instance for your compliance history and calculates the next cycle.

docs.title: How to Configure Advance Notice
docs.text:
To optimize the Smart Status algorithm for your specific business risks, make sure to define the preparation window whenever you create or edit a Job:

  1. Navigate to Items and open an asset.
  2. Click Create Job (or edit an existing one).
  3. Locate the Advance Notice field.
  4. Input a realistic timeframe based on the real-world friction of the task:
    • Routine cleaning/checks: Set to 1 day or 0 days.
    • Vehicle oil changes/inspections: Set to 3 to 5 days.
    • Commercial leases or insurance renewals: Set to 15 to 30 days.
    • Complex legal certifications or passport renewals: Set to 30 to 60 days.
  5. Click Save.

By aligning these notice windows with your actual operational realities, Upkapp turns your dashboard into a self-sorting command center that automatically protects your business from overlooked risks.

docs.title: Templates
docs.text: Setting up an operations or maintenance tracking system from scratch can feel overwhelming. To accelerate your initial setup, Upkapp includes a powerful Templates engine. This allows you to import pre-configured organizational structures instantly, or export your own workflows to share them with other users.

docs.title: What is an Upkapp Template?
docs.text:
A template is a blueprint of a workflow. It packages a ready-made hierarchical structure consisting of Groups, Items, and Jobs into a single configuration.

There are two sources of templates in Upkapp: * System Templates: Standard industry frameworks provided natively by Upkapp (e.g., standard fire safety setups, general fleet checklists).

  • User-Shared Templates: Custom workflows built and shared by other professionals within the Upkapp community.

docs.title: Core Characteristics of Templates
docs.text: Before you begin using templates, it is important to understand how they interact with your account data:

docs.title: Structure Only (No Historical Data)
docs.text: Templates only copy the structural layout and the configuration rules of your jobs. They do not contain historical records, completion logs, or old work orders. Importing a template is an automated pre-configuration tool, not a data migration process.

docs.title: Safe, Non-Destructive Merging
docs.text: When you import a template, Upkapp merges the new structure into your existing account environment. It will never overwrite, substitute, or delete any of your currently registered groups, items, or jobs without explicit user action. It safely appends the template data alongside your current setup.

docs.title: Creating and Sharing Your Own Templates
docs.text:
If you have built an exceptional tracking structure for your business, you can package it into a template to deploy it across other branches or share it with peers.

  1. Navigate to Menu > Templates in the main navigation.
  2. Select the option to Create Template.
  3. Choose the specific Groups, Items, and Jobs you want to include in the blueprint.
  4. Generate the template.
  5. Upkapp will provide you with a unique Template Code. Anyone with this code can instantly replicate your entire workflow structure in their own Upkapp account. You can also unshare or delete a template at any time.

docs.title: Importing and Activating a Template
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Menu > Templates.
  2. Select Import Template and enter the unique template code or choose from the system gallery.
  3. Follow the on-screen instructions to finalize the import.

docs.title: ⚠️ Critical Next Step: Check Your Dates!
docs.text:
Because templates are generic blueprints, they arrive with baseline default dates. The very first thing you must do after importing a template is to audit each new Job and map it to your real-world calendar.

Open the newly imported Jobs, update their parameters, and use the Restarting a Job feature (Save and Restart) to anchor the starting date precisely to your company's actual operational schedule.

docs.title: User Management
docs.text: Upkapp beautifully blends industrial-grade power with everyday simplicity. Managing your team shouldn't require a degree in IT, which is why our user creation process is straightforward while still offering robust control over data visibility and responsibilities.

docs.title: When Creating a User
docs.text:
Adding a team member to Upkapp is quick and intuitive. For every user you onboard, you can customize three key settings:

  • Preferred Language: Upkapp is fully localized. You can set each user's interface independently to either English or Portuguese, allowing an international or diverse team to work seamlessly together.
  • User Type (Role): Defines what actions the user is authorized to perform across the platform.
  • Group Access: Restricts or grants visibility to specific areas of your business. A user will only see Items, Jobs, and Work Orders belonging to the Groups you explicitly check for them.

docs.title: The 3 User Types in Upkapp
docs.text: To keep workflows secure and simple, Upkapp uses three distinct user roles:

docs.title: 1. Master User
docs.text: This is the account creator. The Master user has unrestricted, global access to the entire platform. * Key Responsibilities: Full operational control across all Groups. * Exclusive Permissions: The Master user is the only role capable of modifying billing information, changing subscription plans, and managing other users (creating, editing, or deleting profiles).

docs.title: 2. Manager User
docs.text: Managers are the operational leaders of specific departments or areas. They have full autonomy within their assigned scope. * Key Responsibilities: Within the Groups they have been granted access to, Managers can perform any action. This includes creating new Items, configuring complex Jobs, modifying data, updating meters, and handling assignments. * Limitations: Managers cannot see or modify Groups they don't have access to, and they have absolutely no access to the account's billing or user management settings.

docs.title: 3. Staff User
docs.text: Staff users are your frontline executors. Their interface is stripped of administrative clutter so they can focus purely on getting work done. * Key Responsibilities: Staff users can only view and complete Work Orders within their assigned Groups. * Limitations: They cannot create Groups, Items, or Jobs, nor can they alter core configurations or system data. They log in, look at their prioritized list, execute the tasks, and mark them as done.

docs.title: Expanding Your Team
docs.text:
Your baseline Upkapp subscription includes 5 users right out of the box.

If your business grows and you need to onboard more team members, adding extra user slots is simple. The capability to register additional users depends on your active subscription plan. For details on upgrading your seat capacity or checking current tier limits, please visit the Billing & Subscription page.

docs.title: Work Orders
docs.text:
If Jobs are the rules that define your business operations, Work Orders are the actionable reality. A Work Order is the actual ticket generated by Upkapp that tells your team exactly what needs to be done today.

By automating the generation and prioritization of these tasks, Upkapp ensures nothing is forgotten and your team always executes the right task at the right time.

docs.title: The "Set Once and Let It Run" Philosophy
docs.text:
In traditional systems, managers spend hours every week creating tasks, looking at calendars, and reassigning duties. Upkapp completely eliminates this administrative overhead.

With Upkapp, you set it once and let the system run the show: * You configure a recurring rule just once inside a Job. * Upkapp's engine quietly monitors the dates or Meters in the background. * The exact moment a condition is met, a clean, actionable Work Order appears on the dashboard. * Once a team member completes it, the system logs the history and automatically queues up the next cycle.

You no longer need to spend mental energy remembering to create the next task—Upkapp handles the endless loop of business repetition for you.

docs.title: The Power of Automatic Prioritization
docs.text:
Your daily operations dashboard isn't just a random list of things to do; it is a live, self-sorting command center driven by our Smart Status algorithm.

The advantages of this automatic prioritization include: * Zero Decision Fatigue: Your team doesn't have to guess what to do first. They simply log in and work from the top of the list downward. * Risk Mitigation: High-impact, long-preparation deadlines (like legal permits or passport renewals) are automatically boosted above low-impact daily chores, even if the chore is technically due sooner. * Real-Time Responsiveness: If a metric changes via our API or manual entry, the dashboard adapts instantly, shifting urgent maintenance tasks to the top of the queue.

docs.title: The Lifecycle of a Work Order
docs.text:
Every Work Order flows through a clear, automated pipeline:

Job Triggered ──> Scheduled / Upcoming ──> Active / In Progress ──> Done / Archived

  1. Generation: Upkapp automatically spins up the Work Order based on your Job configuration.
  2. Awareness (Upcoming/Scheduled): The task appears on the dashboard. If it has an advance notice window, it signals the team to prepare.
  3. Execution (Started): The user updates the status to show they are actively working on it.
  4. Completion (Done): The task is finalized, closing the loop and triggering the next cycle.

docs.title: How to Complete a Work Order
docs.text:
We designed the execution interface to be as frictionless as possible so your team actually enjoys using it. Completing a task takes only a few seconds:

  1. Navigate to the Work Orders dashboard.
  2. Click on the active Work Order at the top of your list to view its details and any specific instructions.
  3. click on "action".
  4. Once the real-world work is finished, simply click the Done button.

Depending on your configuration you can - Skip work order - Cancel work order - Mark as "Done at" (if you need to registrate a done task in the past)

The moment Done is clicked, the current Work Order is safely tucked away into your permanent compliance history, and Upkapp instantly evaluates the underlying Job to schedule the next occurrence.
